summary: Creating a Slack app and installing it to your own workspace is instant with no review. Listing it in the Slack Marketplace for anyone to install is a different story — it requires 10+ active installs before you can even submit, then a two-phase review.

decision.question: Will this run in your own workspace only, or get listed for any workspace to install?

options.name: Single workspace
pickWhen: Building for your own team or workspace
You want to start testing immediately
options.tradeoff: Instant, no review — but the app can't be installed by other workspaces.

options.name: Slack Marketplace (public distribution)
pickWhen: Any Slack workspace should be able to install your app
options.tradeoff: Requires 10+ active installs before you can even submit, a two-phase review that can take up to ~12 weeks total, and restricts which scopes you can request.

decision.recommendation: Start with a single-workspace install to build and test. Pursue Marketplace listing only once you have real usage — the install threshold and review timeline make it a late-stage step, not a launch blocker.

difficultyReason: Installing a Slack app to the workspace you created it in requires no review and works immediately. But distributing it publicly via the Slack Marketplace requires 10+ active installs sustained through the whole review, plus a two-phase review process that can take up to roughly 12 weeks.

time.approvalWait: None to install to your own workspace. For Slack Marketplace listing: up to 10 business days for a preliminary review, then up to 10 weeks for the functional review on new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions) — this cannot be expedited.
time.notes: Official docs don't state a hands-on setup time; the estimate above is based on the number of required steps (create app, configure scopes, set redirect URI, install), not a documented figure.

accessCost.pricingModel: Free — the Slack Web API has no usage-based or per-call pricing. A Slack workspace (free or paid tier) is required to develop against, but workspace subscription pricing is separate from API usage.
accessCost.rates: No per-call charges. Subject to per-method rate limits (tiered, roughly 1 to 100+ requests/minute depending on the method).
accessCost.freeTierLimits: No metered usage cap to run out of — only the per-method rate limits apply, regardless of workspace plan.

whenReviewIsNeeded.text: Listing an app in the Slack Marketplace for public distribution requires passing a two-phase review (preliminary, then functional).

requirements.text: A Slack workspace to develop in — your own, or a development sandbox.
A publicly reachable HTTPS redirect URI. Slack rejects plain http:// and any URL containing an anchor (#).

If targeting Marketplace listing: the app must already be installed on 10 or more active workspaces (used within the last 28 days) before submission, sustained throughout the review, and fully tested end-to-end including uninstall on a non-development workspace.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps, click 'Create New App', choose 'From scratch' or 'From an app manifest', and select the workspace to develop in.

steps.title: Configure OAuth scopes
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions, add bot scopes (the app's own identity and permissions, via the scope parameter) and/or user scopes (acting on behalf of a user, via user_scope) depending on what the integration needs.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: Add the HTTPS redirect URI under OAuth & Permissions. It must exactly match — or be a subdirectory of — the URL sent in the authorization request.

steps.title: Install to your workspace
steps.detail: Click 'Install to Workspace' to generate a token and start testing immediately — no review needed for this step.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth redirect and token exchange
steps.detail: Redirect users to Slack's authorize endpoint with the client ID and scopes, then exchange the returned code (valid for 10 minutes) for an access token via oauth.v2.access.

blockers.fix: It must be HTTPS, contain no anchor (#), and exactly match or be a subdirectory of a URL configured under OAuth & Permissions.

blockers.problem: App can't be installed by other workspaces.
blockers.fix: Expected before the app is approved for public distribution — until then it's restricted to the workspace it was created in. The team parameter only becomes a hint (not a restriction) once the app is distributed.

blockers.problem: Marketplace submission rejected before review even starts.
blockers.fix: Reach 10+ active installs (used within the last 28 days) and keep that threshold through the whole review. Fully test the install, setup, and uninstall flow on a non-development workspace first.

agentCanDo: Build the authorization URL with the right scopes
Implement the callback handler and code-for-token exchange
Call Slack Web API methods using the returned token
humanMustDo: Create the app and configure OAuth scopes and redirect URI in the Slack dashboard
If pursuing Marketplace listing: reach the 10-install threshold and handle the review submission
openQuestions: Exact hands-on setup time isn't stated in official docs — the estimate given is based on the number of required steps, not a documented figure.
Whether rate limits or a paid-tier requirement gate any part of OAuth app creation or Marketplace listing isn't addressed in the docs reviewed.
The exact scope list considered 'extensive access' or 'restricted' for Marketplace eligibility, beyond the named examples (admin.*, search:read, triggers:*).
